tema: Investigates trends and factors associated with recurrence and all-cause mortality after ischaemic stroke in a rural US population (2004-2018).
diseno: Retrospective cohort based on electronic health records (GNSIS database); 8561 consecutive patients with ischaemic stroke; stratified Cox and cause-specific hazards models.
hallazgos: Hypertension was the most prevalent factor (75.2%); recurrence and mortality at one year were 6.3% and 16.1%. Recurrence increased and mortality decreased; age > 65, atrial fibrillation or flutter, heart failure and previous stroke predicted mortality, and diabetes, chronic kidney disease and age < 65 years, recurrence.
conclusion: Although mortality after stroke decreased, recurrence and several vascular risk factors increased; more control of risk factors in underserved subpopulations is required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent with each other, but the paper does not deal with ME/CFS; it appears to be a document included in the collection by mistake.

tema: Proposes molecular mechanisms by which neuroinflammation sustains ME/CFS and long COVID and favours relapses.
diseno: Hypothesis article partly supported by own molecular studies (DNA methylome, gene mutations; data in GEO) in cohorts of patients and controls from New Zealand.
hallazgos: After the initial stressor (virus or other), systemic pathology would reach the brain via neurovascular routes or through a dysfunctional BBB, generating chronic neuroinflammation; brain-body signalling would maintain the relapse-recovery cycle. Long COVID would arise through very similar mechanisms with SARS-CoV-2-specific signals.
conclusion: The similarity of symptoms despite the diversity of triggers supports a dysfunctional CNS component common to both diseases, perpetuated by everyday stresses.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (neuroinflammation, relapses, BBB, chronic immune activation). The discussion text is almost all noise (ethics, contributions, funding) and only confirms the role of everyday stresses.

tema: Analyses, using multi-omics, gut microbiome-host interactions in ME/CFS patients of short and long duration.
diseno: Case-control study: 75 ME/CFS patients of short duration (<4 years), 79 of long duration (>10 years) and 79 healthy controls; deep stool metagenomics, plasma metabolomics, clinical phenotyping and classification models.
hallazgos: Short-duration patients showed marked microbial dysbiosis, whereas in long-duration patients it was largely resolved but metabolic and clinical alterations persisted. Lower microbial butyrate biosynthesis and decreased plasma butyrate, bile acids and benzoate were observed.
conclusion: The data reveal possible mechanisms of disease onset and duration and constitute a resource for formulating hypotheses about host-microbiome interactions.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (dysbiosis, metabolomics, bile acids). The conclusions text is only noise (methods, acknowledgements, conflict of interest), so it provides no triangulation.

tema: Compares cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and CFS with multidimensional measures to explore psychophysiological markers that differentiate them.
diseno: Comparative cross-sectional study with 25 CRF patients and 20 with CFS; questionnaires (FSS, HADS, PSS, PSQI), high-sensitivity CRP, heart rate variability (HRV), EEG and neurocognitive assessment.
hallazgos: Both groups had comparable levels of psychological variables, including fatigue. CRF patients had higher hs-CRP and a lower HRV index. In CFS, fatigue was associated with perceived stress and with frontal EEG delta, theta and alpha power.
conclusion: CRF and CFS have different pathophysiological mechanisms; inflammation and HRV could differentiate them and frontal EEG parameters could be quantitative biomarkers of CFS.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract and agree fully. The keywords stress CRP and inflammation, but do not include HRV or EEG, which the study presents as relevant biomarkers.

tema: Evaluates in a multimodal and simultaneous way brain and CSF abnormalities in CFS and whether psychiatric comorbidity modifies them.
diseno: Case-control study with CFS patients with and without psychiatric comorbidity and healthy controls; neuropsychological assessment, CSF proteins and leukocytes, cerebral blood flow, ventricular lactate and cortical glutathione by spectroscopy. Total size not stated (26 patients in the outlier analysis).
hallazgos: There were no differences between patients with and without psychiatric comorbidity. The patient group as a whole showed lower glutathione and cerebral flow, higher ventricular lactate and more CSF abnormalities than controls; 13 of 26 had abnormal values in two or more of the four brain variables.
conclusion: Psychiatric comorbidity does not appear to aggravate CFS; a subgroup shows brain dysfunction that is probably causal, to which the authors propose applying the term myalgic encephalomyelitis.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text and discussion are consistent. The discussion adds limitations (exclusion of medicated patients, incomplete data, possible lack of power) that qualify the absence of differences by psychiatric comorbidity.

tema: Investigates changes in brain structural networks related to autoantibodies against adrenergic and muscarinic receptors in ME/CFS.
diseno: Prospective study in 89 right-handed patients with 3D T1 MRI and titres of anti-β1 AdR, β2 AdR, M3 and M4 AChR antibodies; grey matter similarity networks per subject and local and global properties.
hallazgos: Betweenness centrality correlated positively with β1-AdR-Ab in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and characteristic path length negatively with β2-AdR-Ab in the right precentral gyrus; there were no correlations with volumes or with global properties.
conclusion: The β1 AdR-Ab and β2 AdR-Ab antibodies are potential markers of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The conclusions repeat the final sentence of the abstract word for word, with editorial noise; keywords and abstract agree on structural networks and β receptors. The conclusion about markers is broader than the regional correlations found.

tema: Determines the prevalence of CFS/ME in a US population sample and examines its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD).
diseno: Cross-sectional study with weighted data from 114,834 participants in the 2021-2022 National Health Interview Survey; multivariable logistic regression adjusted for traditional cardiovascular risk factors.
hallazgos: Median age was 53 years and 53.9% were women; the prevalence of CFS/ME was 1.2%. A history of CFS/ME was significantly associated with CVD after adjustment (aOR 3.26; 95% CI 2.85-3.72; p < 0.001).
conclusion: CFS/ME is independently associated with CVD, so patients require careful cardiovascular assessment; more studies on this relationship are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are somewhat more forceful in presenting CFS/ME as an 'independent risk factor', something that a cross-sectional design does not allow to be established causally.

tema: Investigates whether naltrexone restores TRPM3 channel function in NK cells of ME/CFS patients.
diseno: In vitro experimental study with whole-cell patch-clamp in IL-2-stimulated NK cells from 8 ME/CFS patients and 8 age- and sex-matched controls, after modulation with pregnenolone sulphate, naltrexone (24 h) and ononetin.
hallazgos: Impaired TRPM3 function was confirmed in patients' NK cells. Incubation with naltrexone for 24 h restored channel activity, and naltrexone does not act as a direct agonist of the TRPM3 channel.
conclusion: Naltrexone would counteract opioid receptor-mediated inhibition of TRPM3 in NK cells, reshaping the Ca2+ signal, which supports its possible therapeutic use in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on naltrexone, the mu opioid receptor, NK and calcium signalling. The discussion adds the role of immune opioid receptors in analgesia and includes ethics and funding noise; the evidence is in vitro with a small sample.

tema: Evaluates, within the multicentre MCAM study, whether NK cell count and cytotoxicity serve as a biomarker of ME/CFS.
diseno: Multicentre cross-sectional study with 174 ME/CFS patients, 86 healthy controls and 10 sick controls; NK cytotoxicity assay validated for samples shipped overnight and standardized questionnaires.
hallazgos: NK cytotoxicity showed great variability (mean 34.1% in ME/CFS versus 33.6% in controls) with no significant differences (p = 0.79). It was not associated with disease domains, physical or mental well-being, infection history or comorbidities.
conclusion: The NK cytotoxicity assay is not ready for clinical implementation and studies on other immune parameters implicated in the pathophysiology are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent: keywords centred on NK cells and biomarkers, abstract with a negative result and PDF conclusion that reproduces the abstract's word for word.

tema: Explores symptom co-occurrence in Polish CFS patients through network analysis.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 110 CFS patients (75 women; mean age 37.93 years; mean duration 4.4 years); symptom network analysis with CFQ and FIS for fatigue severity.
hallazgos: PEM was present in 75.45%, unrefreshing sleep in 89.09% and memory or concentration impairment in 87.27%. The most connected nodes were total number of symptoms, sore throat and PEM; PEM was related to cognitive impairment and greater fatigue, and sore throat to autonomic dysfunction.
conclusion: The findings show the centrality of PEM in the CFS symptom network and help link the symptomatic presentation with the pathophysiology of specific systems.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on PEM, unrefreshing sleep and memory impairment; the PDF conclusions add a limitations section and perspectives on TRPM3 channels that exceed the results. Its relationship to genetics/omics is tangential.

tema: Determines the neural consequences of acute exercise (PEM) in ME/CFS using functional magnetic resonance imaging.
diseno: Case-control study with 15 women with ME/CFS and 15 controls; 30 min of submaximal exercise (70% of peak HR); symptoms and fMRI one week before and 24 h after during cognitive (PASAT, number recognition) and motor tasks.
hallazgos: Patients had large increases in symptoms, worsened in cognitive performance after exercise versus the improvement of controls, and showed greater activity in parietal and cingulate cortices during the PASAT, related to symptoms.
conclusion: Acute exercise exacerbated symptoms, altered cognition and brain function, providing objective evidence of harmful neurophysiological effects of PEM and of brain fog.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions place the findings in the literature on the central nervous system and stress the importance of symptom provocation.

tema: Analyses the function of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and thyroid in women of reproductive age with CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 40 women with CFS and 40 healthy women (15-45 years); serum cortisol at 08:00 and 18:00, ACTH, T4, T3 and TSH; fatigue measured with the Fibro Fatigue Scale.
hallazgos: Cortisol levels were normal in both groups, but the positive correlation between morning and evening cortisol present in healthy women was missing in the CFS group. T4, T3 and TSH were in the normal range, although T3 was significantly lower in CFS.
conclusion: A single hormone measurement is not enough to detect imbalances; the absence of correlation between morning and evening cortisol could be a more representative indicator of HPA axis alteration.
triangulacion: Keywords (HPA axis, diurnal cortisol rhythm, T3), abstract and conclusions (taken from the structured abstract) agree; the conclusions add no independent information.

tema: Reviews faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) observations that implicate 11 gut bacteria in IBS and associated fatigue.
diseno: Narrative review based on FMT studies in IBS patients. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Nine bacteria (e.g., Alistipes, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Prevotella, Lactobacillus) increased after FMT with inverse correlation with symptoms and fatigue; two (Streptococcus thermophilus, Coprobacillus cateniformis) decreased. Several produce short-chain fatty acids, especially butyrate.
conclusion: If confirmed, these bacteria could be used as probiotics and diets rich in animal protein or in vegetables could modulate them; Alistipes could be a biomarker of FMT response.
triangulacion: Coherence among the three sources. The conclusions (from the discussion) warn about probiotics with S. thermophilus. The focus is IBS with chronic fatigue, not ME/CFS proper.

tema: Identifies which brain abnormalities in ME/CFS are observed consistently or inconsistently across neuroimaging studies.
diseno: Retrospective systematic review in Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed and Scopus (1988-2018); qualitative synthesis of 63 articles out of 291 identified.
hallazgos: Recruitment of additional areas in cognitive tasks (11 studies) and brainstem abnormalities (9 studies) are frequent; slow BOLD response, reduction of serotonin transporters and regional hypometabolism are consistent, and reduced resting flow and volumetric changes inconsistent.
conclusion: The findings suggest abnormal neurovascular coupling and autonomic dysfunction of possible central origin; the authors point out small samples and propose a neuroimaging data bank.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on reproducibility and neurovascular coupling; the conclusions add autonomic dysfunction and the methodological criticisms.

tema: Critical review of the methods for studying neuroinflammation in ME/CFS: TSPO PET, MRS and cytokines in blood and CSF.
diseno: Critical narrative literature review; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: PET with TSPO radioligands is promising but has methodological difficulties; most studies do not use optimal techniques for the brainstem; MRS is less informative but more accessible. Biological and methodological variability explains the lack of replication of cytokine profiles.
conclusion: A replicable diagnostic cytokine profile is unlikely to be found; the field must overcome the defensive stance and focus on mechanisms, choosing ROIs according to the neuroinflammation literature and controlling for confounding factors.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on neuroinflammation, TSPO, MRS and cytokines; the conclusions add methodological recommendations and a critique of the descriptive approach of the field.

tema: Reviews how neuroinflammation without brain damage, exacerbated by environmental stressors, can underlie chronic illness behaviour disorders such as ME/CFS and Gulf War illness.
diseno: Narrative review of experimental and clinical literature on neuroinflammation, sickness behaviour and the role of stress hormones (corticosterone).
hallazgos: Describes that the acute-phase inflammatory response induces sickness behaviour (fatigue, myalgia, cognitive problems) and that recurrent or chronic forms can occur without an underlying cause. Points out that HPA axis activation can prime neuroinflammation in response to later challenges.
conclusion: Neuroinflammation without brain damage may be due to disparate exposures, and recurrent environmental stressors could exacerbate and prolong chronic inflammatory disorders; its complexity hinders therapeutic development.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text (the abstract includes the article header) and the final summary of the discussion are consistent around neuroinflammation and stressors; the discussion adds uncertainty about the timing of corticosterone supplementation and includes noise from acknowledgements and funding.

tema: Evaluates the efficacy of the AIR neuroplasticity programme (amygdala and insula retraining) on health and functioning in various chronic conditions.
diseno: Exploratory cross-sectional study with self-report after 3 or more months of using AIR; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Self-reported wellbeing increased significantly in 14 conditions (including ME/CFS, fibromyalgia and long COVID, according to the opening text) with medium to large effect sizes.
conclusion: AIR could be a valuable and low-cost resource, although randomized controlled trials are required to establish causality.
triangulacion: There are no keywords; the abstract is opening text (introduction) and the conclusions are enthusiastic ('potentially revolutionary') despite the self-reported cross-sectional design, which limits their robustness.

tema: Tests whether neurovascular dysregulation underlies exercise intolerance in ME/CFS through cholinergic stimulation with pyridostigmine.
diseno: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled single-centre trial; 45 ME/CFS patients (23 pyridostigmine 60 mg, 22 placebo) after an iCPET, with a second iCPET 50 min later; primary outcome: peak VO2.
hallazgos: The abstract's results are not stated (truncated opening text). According to the discussion, pyridostigmine improved aerobic capacity by increasing cardiac output through greater right ventricular preload, and with placebo peak VO2, cardiac output and right atrial pressure decreased.
conclusion: Neurovascular dysregulation underlies acute exercise intolerance in ME/CFS; the decline after placebo suggests a physiological mechanism of PEM.
triangulacion: The abstract is opening text truncated before the results, so the conclusion depends on the discussion. Keywords (pyridostigmine, cholinergic stimulation, peak VO2, cardiac output) are consistent with both.

tema: Describes the treatment of a long COVID patient with BC 007, a DNA aptamer that neutralizes autoantibodies against G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR-AAbs).
diseno: Case report of a patient with prior glaucoma, mild COVID-19 and subsequent CFS, ageusia and impaired retinal capillary microcirculation; evaluation with OCT angiography and functional determination of GPCR-AAbs before and after a single dose of BC 007.
hallazgos: At 48 h after a single administration the GPCR-AAbs were functionally inactivated and remained so for 4 weeks of observation, with steady improvement of fatigue, taste and macular and peripapillary capillary microcirculation.
conclusion: The authors propose that elimination of GPCR-AAbs could improve features of post-COVID syndrome such as capillary alteration, loss of taste and CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (long COVID, aptamers, autoantibody neutralization). The conclusions text comes from the discussion and only contains OCT-A methods and ethical declarations, so it provides no conclusions of its own; the evidence is from a single case.

tema: Characterizes mast cell phenotypes in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of CFS/ME patients and healthy controls, and the expression of HMGB1 and RAGE.
diseno: Preliminary case-control study: 12 moderate patients, 6 severe (ICC 2011 criteria) and 13 controls; flow cytometry with lineage and inclusion markers (CD117, CD34, FcεRI, chymase, HLA-DR, CD154) and ELISA for HMGB1 and sRAGE.
hallazgos: Significant increase in CD117+CD34+FcεRI-chymase- populations (mast cell progenitors) in moderate and severe patients versus controls, and higher expression of CD40 ligand and MHC-II in mast cells differentiated from severe patients. No differences in HMGB1 or sRAGE.
conclusion: Peripheral mast cells could participate in the pathology of CFS/ME, but more research is required, including on neuroinflammatory processes and the blood-brain barrier.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the increase in progenitors and activated mast cells; the PDF conclusions are somewhat more assertive ('we discovered for the first time activated mast cells') than the abstract, which stresses the preliminary nature.

tema: Evaluates whether the head-up tilt test (HUT) triggers prolonged post-exertional symptoms in ME/CFS, with and without fibromyalgia.
diseno: Study with 174 ME/CFS patients with fibromyalgia, 104 without fibromyalgia and 30 controls; numeric rating scales (NRS) of pain, fatigue and concentration before, immediately after, at 24 h, 48 h and 7 days after HUT.
hallazgos: In controls there were no changes; in both patient groups the three NRS remained elevated even at 7 days. Pain was higher with fibromyalgia; fatigue and concentration peaked right after HUT and pain at 24 h.
conclusion: Orthostatic stress is an important determinant of PEM.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are fully consistent; the PDF conclusions faithfully summarize the abstract without adding nuances.

tema: Presents clinical phenotypes and one-year follow-up of German adolescents and young adults with ME/CFS after EBV infectious mononucleosis.
diseno: Prospective cohort of 12 adolescents and 13 young adults diagnosed at a tertiary service (criteria with mandatory PEM and confirmed EBV primary infection); laboratory, symptom, physical function and quality of life assessment at 0, 6 and 12 months.
hallazgos: Young adults had more severe symptoms and worsened; at one year, 6 of 12 adolescents no longer met criteria, whereas all young adults still met the Canadian ones. EBV serology and DNA load did not correlate with the clinical picture and there were no signs of inflammation; the median time to diagnosis was 13.8 months.
conclusion: ME/CFS after EBV mononucleosis is highly disabling, is diagnosed late and responds poorly to conventional care, especially in adults; there is no evidence that EBV perpetuates the disease and biomarkers and treatments are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent; the PDF explicitly adds that there is no evidence of perpetuation by EBV and highlights the barriers to access to care.

tema: Evaluates a treatment targeting gut dysbiosis (erythromycin and a probiotic) on neuropsychological symptoms in ME/CFS and compares by sex.
diseno: Open repeated-measures pilot trial: 44 adults with ME/CFS (27 women) from a clinic, with Streptococcus overgrowth; 4 weeks alternating erythromycin and a D-lactate-free probiotic; 2x2 ANOVA and correlations.
hallazgos: Streptococcus counts were reduced and total symptoms, some sleep parameters and cognitive functions (attention, processing speed, flexibility, memory, fluency) improved. Mood, fatigue and the D:L-lactate ratio did not change; microbial changes explained more clinical variance in men.
conclusion: Specific microorganisms interact with some symptoms and addressing dysbiosis is promising, although Streptococcus would not be the main producer of D-lactate and sequencing is required before a placebo-controlled trial.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions are more cautious: they question the D-lactate premise and propose other mechanisms (immunomodulation by macrolides and probiotics).

tema: Evaluates whether the NASA Lean Test aggravates symptoms and produces objective haemodynamic and cognitive alterations in long COVID and ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 42 long COVID patients, 26 with ME/CFS and 20 healthy controls; 10-min NASA Lean Test and cognitive assessment with a mobile app before, during, immediately after, and at 2 and 7 days.
hallazgos: The test worsened symptoms only in the patient groups; it provoked a progressive narrowing of pulse pressure, especially in long COVID, and worsened reaction times, especially procedural reaction.
conclusion: A simple in-office orthostatic test and a cognitive app can objectively confirm the OI and brain fog of both groups; the authors stress the importance of detecting it early.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on OI, brain fog and long COVID; the conclusions add that early treatment could theoretically prevent chronification, raised as a hypothesis.

tema: Compares orthostatic symptoms and cerebral blood flow reduction between long COVID, ME/CFS and healthy controls.
diseno: Study with 10 long COVID patients, 20 controls with ME/CFS and POTS, 20 with ME/CFS and normal haemodynamic response and 10 matched healthy individuals; same questionnaires and tilt test with CBF and cardiac index.
hallazgos: There were no differences in prevalence of ME/CFS symptoms between long COVID and ME/CFS; all long COVID patients developed POTS. CBF and cardiac index were reduced more in the three patient groups than in healthy individuals, and CBF reduction was greater in long COVID than in ME/CFS with a normal response.
conclusion: Long COVID resembles ME/CFS; the early onset of OI in previously active people makes it unlikely that POTS is due to deconditioning, and SARS-CoV-2 would act as a trigger for ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions are consistent; the keywords do not mention long COVID, which is the central focus, although they do reflect POTS, CBF and cardiac index.
